summary: Modoc-area lookout station near Bieber, active by 1937 and reviewed in 1947; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: lookout observation unit with living quarters underneath, plus a one-car garage (1944 plan)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed and gone; no source describes what remains on the site.

events.note: CCC spike camp set up in June 1937 to build a road from Hayden Hill to the Boyd Mountain station, with a telephone line planned
Planned: guard G.M. Johnson to be stationed at Boyd Mountain that summer
Season review said the station was not paying its way; said moving detection to Mahogany Ridge should be seriously considered and that a fire crew setup should replace the station
Gerig fire threatened the Boyd Hill Lookout; firefighters averted damage to it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1937 notice calls the station Boyd Mountain; the 1944 plan and the rest of the page use Boyd Hill, so the two names appear to refer to the same station.

notes_for_editor: Almost all history comes from one page (Kemnow), which quotes 1937-1977 notices and Forest Service documents. Two Forest Service PDFs and a 1945 Modoc history were unreachable this session (timeouts, 504, connection refused); a re-check may add build date and removal date. Build year unknown; the 1937 notice implies the station existed by then. Kind enclosed_tower comes from the FFLA list; the 1944 plan (observation unit with living quarters underneath) does not contradict it but does not settle the design. Removal date and cause unknown. Access and visit facts left out: no source.
